q: All metals have a tendency to lose electrons and form metal ions.
e: True. All metals have a tendency to lose electrons and form metal ions.

q: All metals are good oxidizing agents and easily reduced by themselves.
e: False. All metals are good oxidizing agents and easily oxidised by themselves. An oxidising agent is the species that is reduced. it takes electrons from something else.

q: The reactivity series of metals is a series in which metals are arranged in order of reactivity from lowest to highest.
e: False. The reactivity series of metals is a series in which metals are arranged in order of reactivity from lowest to lowest. The reactivity series ranks metals from most reactive to least reactive.

q: Metals above carbon can only be extracted from their ores by electrolysis.
e: True. Metals above carbon can only be extracted from their ores by electrolysis. Metals above carbon are too reactive for carbon reduction, so they are extracted by electrolysis. Metals above carbon in the series cannot be smelted with carbon and need electrolysis.

q: Metals below hydrogen can react vigorously with water and acids.
e: False. Potassium and sodium react violently with cold water, float, and catch fire. Metals below hydrogen do not displace hydrogen from water or acid and are hard to oxidise. Metals below hydrogen can react vigorously with water and acids.

q: Potassium and sodium are very reactive and never found as free elements.

q: The reactions of metals with dilute acids produce the corresponding metallic salts and oxygen gas.

q: Displacement reaction is a chemical reaction in which a less reactive metal displaces a more reactive metal from its compound.
e: False. Dehydrogenation is a chemical reaction in which hydrogen is removed from a compound. Displacement reaction is a chemical reaction in which a less reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from its compound.

q: When a piece of magnesium is placed in a copper(II) sulphate solution, a brown solid forms on the surface of magnesium.
e: True. When a piece of magnesium is placed in a copper(II) sulphate solution, a brown solid forms on the surface of magnesium. Copper(II) sulphate solution is a common electrolyte, and hydrated CuSO4·5H2O is blue.

q: In the displacement reaction between a metal and metal oxide, the less reactive metal will take the oxygen atom from the more reactive metal oxide.
e: False. In the displacement reaction between a metal and metal oxide, the less reactive metal will take the oxygen atom from the less reactive metal oxide. The less reactive metal will take the oxygen atom from the more reactive metal oxide.
